one_liner: Small dependency-free ARM CPU CNN inference library; 2017 wiki shows 2-13x lower latency than Caffe+OpenBLAS and Caffe2+Eigen.
what_it_does: Runs float32 inference of Caffe-style CNNs (VGG, GoogleNet, ResNet, SqueezeNet, MobileNet, DenseNet) on ARM CPUs for Android, iOS and Linux, with an AVX2 x86 backend added in 2019. The current master API is ncnn-like: feather::Net::LoadParam / LoadWeights, FeedInput(name, ncnn::Mat), Forward(), Extract(blob). It is a separate runtime with its own model files, not a drop-in for Caffe, Caffe2 or TFLite.
how_it_is_fast: 3x3 stride-1 convolutions use Winograd F(6x6,3x3) (F(2x2,3x3) also exists), with the transformed tiles multiplied by a batched GEMM the TPDS paper calls TensorGEMM. Other convolutions use im2col plus a hand-written NEON SGEMM (4x12 and 8x12 register-blocked micro-kernels using vfmaq_f32), and depthwise layers get a dedicated kernel. A ReLU that follows a convolution is fused into it, and activations come from a shared memory pool.
when_to_use: Reading the Winograd F(6x6,3x3) and NEON GEMM kernels (src/booster/arm) as BSD-3 reference code for your own ARM convolution work.

Float32 inference of a classic Caffe CNN built only from conv, depthwise conv, pooling, ReLU, BN/Scale, inner product, eltwise, concat and softmax on an ARMv8 phone or board, where you can accept an unmaintained library.
VGG-style networks dominated by 3x3 stride-1 convolutions, where the Winograd path does most of the work (the largest gains on the wiki are for VGG-16).
when_not_to_use: Any new production deployment: there have been no commits since 2019-09-24, open issues (segfault on SqueezeNet, unregistered Deconvolution layer, build failures) have no maintainer replies, and MNN, ncnn or XNNPACK cover the same ground and are maintained.
Models that need ops outside the 13 registered layers (no Deconvolution, Reshape, Permute, detection or SSD layers), partial group convolution, or anything other than fp32 (no int8 or fp16).

Choosing on the wiki numbers: they were measured on the pre-April-2019 code (the .feathermodel / InitFromPath API the README still describes) against Caffe, Caffe2 and TFLite builds from late 2017, and the code was rewritten on master after that.
Multi-core inference through the public API: on master Net() hard-codes one thread and exposes no setter, unlike the per-thread-count tables on the wiki.

integration.dependencies: none for the library (OpenMP optional, GCD on iOS); the Caffe model converter described in the README needs protobuf
integration.min_toolchain: C++11, CMake 2.8; Android NDK (android-21 for arm64-v8a, android-16 for armeabi-v7a) or the Xcode iOS SDK
integration.platforms: aarch64 and armv7 with NEON (Android, iOS, Linux); x86-64 with AVX2 via the BOOSTER_AVX backend (built with -march=core-avx2)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; a Net owns mutable layer buffers and a shared memory pool, so treat one Net as single-threaded

gotchas: The README is stale: it documents Net(num_threads), InitFromPath(.feathermodel) and Forward(float*), while master's net.h has Net(), LoadParam/LoadWeights and ncnn::Mat inputs (the param parser comes from bundled ncnn code).
The top-level CMakeLists adds -Ofast and -ffast-math globally, so results may differ slightly from strict IEEE fp32.
ConvLayer::Forward on master calls printf("thread num =%d") on every convolution, which is debug output left in the hot path.

build_scripts/build_android.sh passes -DCOMPILE_OPENCL=1, which adds src/booster/cl, but that directory is not in master (its CMakeLists.txt returns 404), so expect to edit the script before the Android build works.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick MNN over this for any real ARM deployment: it is maintained, supports far more ops and has its own peer-reviewed (MLSys 2020) comparison against TFLite and ncnn. FeatherCNN is worth taking over NNPACK only as compact BSD-3 reference code for Winograd F(6x6,3x3) with a batched GEMM, not as a runtime.
verified_claims_summary: The first-party wiki reports whole-network fp32 inference time on ARM CPUs measured in late 2017. On a 64-core Huawei D05 (Cortex-A72), best time at any thread count gives VGG-16 102 ms vs 1108 ms for Caffe+OpenBLAS and 1310 ms for Caffe2+Eigen. On an iPhone 7 with 2 cores, VGG-16 runs in 284 ms vs 905 ms for TensorFlow Lite, and on an Nvidia TX2 in 706 ms vs 3569 ms for Caffe2+NNPACK. No compiler, flags or benchmark harness are published, and the wiki's own GoogleNet speedup column (13.7x) disagrees with its timing tables (about 6.6x, derived from page data).
status_note: Abandoned since 2019-09-24, and the README does not match the rewritten master code. BSD-3-Clause source headers make the ARM kernels copyable, but treat it as reference code rather than a runtime to adopt.
